Ivy Nakamura: Heads up — after upgrading the JS SDK our Vite-built edge bundle started crashing with `ReferenceError: Headers is not defined` only in prod. Local dev works.

Ivy Nakamura: stack shows the error originates from a small file in the SDK that polyfills Headers when `globalThis.Headers` is missing.

Omar Ali: do you have `sideEffects: false` in your app package.json? Bundlers can tree-shake top-level side-effect imports.

Ivy Nakamura: yes, app has `sideEffects: false`. SDK v3.0.0 added `dist/edge/init.js` which is only imported for side-effects from `dist/index.mjs`. Looks exactly like a tree-shake case.

Riley Fox: classic — polyfill-only modules get dropped. Quick fix: explicitly import the init file in your edge entry: `import 'redwood-inference-js/dist/edge/init.js'`. Ugly but works.

Ivy Nakamura: confirmed explicit import fixes prod. Bundle increased ~1.8KB.

Omar Ali: SDK-side fixes: mark the specific file in package.json `sideEffects` array, publish an `edge` entry in exports map, or provide an explicit `initEdge()` named export.

Riley Fox: also watch ESM/CJS interop — if the SDK mixes CJS shims the bundler may duplicate code and break prototype augmentation. Tests should include small Vite/Next builds.

Ivy Nakamura: opened internal issue RW-4620 with repro snippet and bundle trace: https://redwood.internal/issue/RW-4620

DevEx Bot: Created ticket RW-4620: "Edge polyfill module tree-shaken when consumer uses sideEffects:false -> runtime error" — https://redwood.internal/issue/RW-4620

Omar Ali: tagging @eng-runtime to consider `exports` map + sideEffects whitelist in next patch.

Ivy Nakamura: adding note to onboarding docs about bundler gotchas (sideEffects:false + implicit polyfills).
